items.entity: design domain orientation / aspect ratio (30×60 elements)
items.description: Fig. 1(a) and Fig. 2 captions give only '30×60 elements' and never say which count lies along the span (horizontal). 'Left boundary fixed' and 'load at lower-right corner' work for either orientation, and the figure isn't available. A cantilever is usually longer than it is tall, but the text doesn't confirm that.

No physical lengths are given for the 2-D cantilever, only element counts (Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 3.1). The filter radius is given in element sizes, which implies square elements, but their absolute size is never stated.
The thickness of the plane model is not specified anywhere (Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 3.1, App. A).

items.entity: which boundary carries the downward load at the lower-right corner
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption: 'a downward distributed load of 1 N is applied at the lower-right corner'. A distributed load can't sit exactly at a corner, and the text doesn't say whether it runs up the right edge, along the bottom edge, or around the corner node. Only the unavailable figure would show this.
readings: on the right (free) edge, starting at the bottom-right corner and extending upward
on the bottom edge, starting at the bottom-right corner and extending leftward
centred on the bottom-right corner node, shared by both edges

items.entity: length and nodal weighting of the 'distributed' corner load
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption calls the load 'distributed' but gives neither the loaded length (number of nodes or element edges) nor the profile (uniform with consistent nodal weights vs. equal nodal shares). This is only shown in the unavailable Fig. 1(a).
readings: 2 element edges (3 nodes; consistent weights 1/4-1/2-1/4 or equal thirds)
about 3–6 element edges (≈10–20% of the 30-element edge)

items.entity: meaning of the '1 N' value of the distributed load
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption gives '1 N' for a distributed load but doesn't say whether that is the resultant, the force per loaded node, or an intensity per element length.
readings: 1 N total resultant shared by the loaded nodes
1 N applied to each loaded node
1 N per unit length (per element edge)

items.entity: non-design (passive solid/void) elements, e.g. a pad at the loaded corner
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption only calls the design domain 'dark gray'. Elsewhere (Figs. 14, 17) light gray marks non-design regions, and the text never says whether the cantilever has any passive elements, such as a solid pad under the load.
readings: none: all 30×60 elements are design variables
small passive solid pad (e.g. 2×2 to 3×3 elements) at the loaded lower-right corner
non-design light-gray block outside the 30×60 grid that carries the load

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid phase
items.description: No elastic modulus is given anywhere (Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 2, Sec. 3.1, App. A).
Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere in the paper.

items.entity: 2-D stress state (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: Sec. 2 and Sec. 3.1 only say 'linear elasticity'. Plane stress vs. plane strain is not stated.
SIMP comes up only as 'common practice' in the Introduction. Neither the interpolation actually used nor its penalty exponent (or any continuation) is given for Fig. 1.
Sec. 2 sets ρ_min = ε with 'e.g., ε ≈ 10^-6', which is only an example. It also doesn't say whether this is a bound on the design variables with E = ρ^p E0 or a modified-SIMP E_min.
readings: ρ_min = 1e-6 bound on design variables, E = ρ^p E0
ρ in [0,1] with E = E_min + ρ^p (E0 − E_min), E_min = 1e-9 E0

items.description: Fig. 1/2 captions and Sec. 3.1 give only 'density-filter radius 2.5 (element size)'. They don't specify the weighting function, how the radius is measured, or what happens at the domain edges.
readings: linear cone (hat) weights max(0, 2.5 − d) on centre-to-centre distance, no padding (top88-style)
linear cone weights with padded/mirrored boundary
Helmholtz PDE filter equivalent to R = 2.5 (r = R/(2√3))

items.entity: MMA move limit η_max (value and schedule) for the Fig. 1 run
items.description: The Fig. 1 caption doesn't give the MMA move limit. The Fig. 3 caption says its setup 'follows Fig. 1(a), except that η_max is reduced to 0.01 after the fifth iteration' (which causes 'minor differences in the optimal material distribution'), implying a constant value for Fig. 1. However, 0.2 is stated only for the Fig. 10/14 runs and Fig. 21. Sec. 3.1 also says the optimal solutions 'use the same numerical settings as in Fig. 3', which blurs things further.

items.entity: remaining MMA parameters and objective scaling
items.description: Sec. 3 and App. A only cite 'the original MMA code by Svanberg'. Asymptote parameters, the a0/a/c/d constants, and any scaling of the compliance objective (MMA is not scale-invariant) aren't given.
readings: Svanberg defaults (a0=1, a=0, c=1000, d=0; asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7) with compliance normalized by its initial value
same defaults with d=1 and compliance multiplied by a fixed factor (e.g. 100)

items.description: The Fig. 1 caption gives only 'maximum iterations, 100'. It's not stated whether a design-change or objective tolerance can stop the run earlier.
readings: stop when max |Δρ| < 0.01, capped at 100 iterations
stop when relative compliance change < 1e-4, capped at 100 iterations

items.entity: density field on which the 0.5 volume constraint is imposed
items.description: Eq. (13) writes the volume constraint on the design variables ρ_e. Sec. 3, however, says the density filter is applied to the design variables in the standard runs (Figs. 1, 2). So it isn't explicit whether 0.5 constrains filtered or raw densities, which differ near the boundaries with an unpadded filter.
Only '30×60 elements' is given (Fig. 1/2 captions). The element formulation and integration rule aren't stated, and App. A only says the codes are 'informed by' open-source codes.
